main_text.p: Sed ob tumultus bellicos frumentorum aliarumq; rerum pretium plus justo adauctum, annonaeq; caritas major.
Sed quid memorem Africae, Asiaeque loca quaedam fœcunditate adeo nobilitata ab autoribus gravissimis, ut fidem pene excedat omnem.Quarundam terrarum ad stuporem usq; mirabilis fœcunditas.

Inprimis vero Babylonica felicitas commendatur. Etenim, Theophrasto prodente, bis illic in anno semper & quasi ordinate tondent triticum, tertio vero pecus admittunt, sic enim caulem mittit, cum alioquin foliis tantum lasciviat. Quid? quod negligentius colentibus quinquagesimo cum fœnore messes reddunt, diligentius vero cum centesimo quinquagesimo.Babylonica fœcunditas. Refert Curtius inter Tygrim & Euphratem jacentia tam vberi & pingui esse solo, vt à pastu repelli pecora dicantur, ne suffocentur. Caufam memorandæ huius fertilitatis tradit, humorem ex vtroque manantem amne per certas aquarum venas.

Theophr. Asiae quodam in loco adeo grande frumentum produci ait, vt grana singula magnitudine sua olivæ nucleis æquiparentur, illicq; omnia rore coalescere. Mirabile dictu & auditu, q; Procurator in Byzantia Africae campo Divo Augusto ex eo loco misit ex vno gra-no quadringenta paucis minus germina.Campus Byzanti-nus fertilissimus. page.notes: Pages in the scan are slightly tilted, and the edges are dark. The marks "q;" before "Procurator" and the word "Cotinet" are doubtful; the mark may be a q with a stroke, and the word may be "Continet" with a tilde. Printed "messes" was read as "messes". Printed "lasciuiat" was normalised to "lasciviat" for the u/v rule. Printed "Diuo" was normalised to "Divo". Printed "oliuę" was normalised to "olivæ". The page ends on the hyphenated word "ferti-", which continues on the next page.
